ja: 町は工事で孤立してる。
en: The town's isolated by roadwork.
alternatives: Roadwork has left the town isolated.
The town has been isolated by construction.
point: isolated は交通などを断たれて孤立した状態。

ja: 週末は、家でのんびりしてたよ。
en: I spent the weekend just lounging around.
alternatives: I just lounged around at home all weekend.
I spent the weekend relaxing at home.
point: spend + 時間 + 〜ing の形

ja: 明日は雨だって聞いたよ。
en: I heard it'll rain tomorrow.
alternatives: I heard it's going to rain tomorrow.
I heard it's supposed to rain tomorrow.
point: heard の後ろの that は省略できる

ja: 自転車を買ったんだ。
en: I got a bike.
alternatives: I bought a bike.
I bought myself a bike.
point: 数えられる名詞には a を付ける

ja: 君、最近何を読んだ？
en: What have you read lately?
alternatives: What did you read recently?
What books have you read recently?
point: lately と現在完了で最近の読書を尋ねる。

ja: 今週末、花火大会があるよ。
en: There's a fireworks show this weekend.
alternatives: There's a fireworks festival this weekend.
They're having a fireworks show this weekend.
point: 「花火大会」は fireworks show / festival

ja: 彼が引っ越してたら今は心の支えがない。
en: If he'd moved, he'd feel unmoored now.
alternatives: Had he relocated, he'd feel adrift now.
If he'd moved, he'd feel emotionally unanchored now.
point: unmoored は心のよりどころを失った比喩。

ja: 帰ったら私に電話して。
en: Call me when you return.
alternatives: Phone me when you get back.
Call me once you get home.
point: 未来の帰宅でも when 節は現在形。

ja: 気乗りしなくても私も行くよ。
en: Reluctant or not, I'll tag along.
alternatives: I'll come along even if I'm reluctant.
I'll come along despite not feeling keen.
point: tag along は他の人について一緒に行く。

ja: ここに人が来る理由、分かる？
en: Do you know what draws people here?
alternatives: Do you know why people come here?
Any idea what attracts people here?
point: 間接疑問は what draws の語順。

ja: うちの犬は雨が嫌いなの。
en: My dog hates the rain.
alternatives: My dog doesn't like rain.
My dog hates rain.
point: 三人称単数の現在形は動詞に s

ja: 晴れたら散歩しようよ。
en: If it's sunny, let's walk.
alternatives: Let's walk if it's sunny.
If it's sunny, let's go walking.
point: if 節の中は未来でも現在形

ja: 私が雑談を切り上げていい？
en: Could I wrap up our conversation?
alternatives: Could I end our chat?
May I finish our conversation?
point: wrap up は話を終わりにする。

ja: 私が気になるのは隣人たちの冷淡さ。
en: What bothers me is the neighbors' aloofness.
alternatives: The neighbors' aloofness is what concerns me.
I'm bothered by how distant the neighbors seem.
point: aloofness は距離を置いて打ち解けない様子。

ja: 偶然会ったのは、同級生なんだ。
en: It was a classmate I bumped into.
alternatives: It was a classmate that I ran into.
The person I ran into was a classmate.
point: It was ～ that 型。that は省略可。bump into は偶然会う

ja: 知ってたら、行ったのに。
en: If I'd known, I'd have come.
alternatives: I'd have come if I'd known.
Had I known, I'd have come.
If I had known, I would have come.
point: 過去の仮定は would have + 過去分詞

ja: 土曜は映画を観たよ。
en: I saw a movie Saturday.
alternatives: I saw a movie on Saturday.
I watched a movie on Saturday.
point: 過去の日付が分かれば過去形

ja: 君が言ってたお店、閉店したらしいよ。
en: I hear the place you mentioned closed down.
alternatives: Apparently the place you mentioned has closed.
I heard the restaurant you told me about closed.
point: 名詞の後の that は省略できる

ja: 隣人は私に騒音を我慢してほしい。
en: My neighbor wants me to tolerate the racket.
alternatives: My neighbor wants me to endure the noise.
My neighbor wants me to bear the racket.
point: racket は迷惑な大きな音。

ja: 今日、ちょっと蒸し暑くない？
en: Doesn't it feel a bit muggy today?
alternatives: Isn't it a little humid today?
Don't you think it's kind of muggy?
point: a bit と否定疑問で柔らかく同意を誘う

ja: 今日は天気がいいね。
en: It's a nice day.
alternatives: The weather is nice today.
It's nice out today.
point: 天気は it を主語にして言う

ja: 今日の暑さは昨日よりずっとまし。
en: Today's heat is far more bearable than yesterday's.
alternatives: Today's heat is much more tolerable than yesterday's.
Yesterday's heat was far less bearable than today's.
point: bearable は暑さなどが我慢できる程度という意味。

ja: 見て、虹だよ！
en: Look at the rainbow!
alternatives: Look at that rainbow!
Look, a rainbow!
Check out the rainbow!
point: 「見て」は look at。see ではない

ja: 傘は持っていくといいよ。
en: You should take an umbrella.
alternatives: You might want to take an umbrella.
You should bring an umbrella with you.
point: 助言は should。had better は強め

ja: 暖かければ、外で食べるのに。
en: If it were warmer, we'd eat outside.
alternatives: We'd have lunch outside if it were warmer.
If it were any warmer, we'd eat outside.
point: if 節は were、主節は would + 動詞

ja: 私はこの週末にくつろげばよかった。
en: I wish I'd unwound this weekend.
alternatives: I wish I'd relaxed this weekend.
If only I'd relaxed this weekend.
point: unwind は緊張を解いてくつろぐ。

ja: 我々が粘れば雨をやり過ごせたのに。
en: If we'd persisted, we'd have weathered the rain.
alternatives: Had we persisted, we'd have weathered the rain.
We'd have weathered the rain had we persisted.
point: weather the rain は雨が収まるまで持ちこたえる。

ja: 私たちが座った途端、雨が降り出した。
en: Hardly had we sat down when it poured.
alternatives: No sooner had we sat down than it poured.
As soon as we sat down, it began to pour.
point: Hardly のあとは had we の倒置。when が続く

ja: 私は明日体を休めるよ。
en: I'll rest tomorrow.
alternatives: I'm going to rest tomorrow.
I plan to rest tomorrow.
point: will でこれから休む予定を伝える。

ja: 花火、見ればよかったなあ。
en: I wish I'd seen the fireworks.
alternatives: If only I'd seen the fireworks.
I wish I had watched the fireworks.
point: 過去への後悔は wish + 過去完了

ja: 私、泳ぎは得意だよ。
en: I can swim well.
alternatives: I'm a good swimmer.
I'm good at swimming.
I swim well.
point: 「得意」は can + 動詞 + well で言える

ja: 私は気まぐれに出かけ続けてる。
en: I've been venturing out spontaneously.
alternatives: I've been going out on a whim.
I've been making spontaneous outings.
point: spontaneously は思いつくままに、その場の気持ちで。

ja: 私はその頃もう社交に疲れ切ってた。
en: I'd burned out socially by then.
alternatives: I'd exhausted myself socializing by then.
I'd worn myself out socially by then.
point: burn out は消耗し切って気力を失う。

ja: 予報だと、晴れると言っていた。
en: The forecast said it'd clear up.
alternatives: The weatherman said it would clear up.
The forecast said it would be sunny.
point: said に合わせて will は would、clear up は「晴れる」

ja: 彼は料理が上手なんだ。
en: He's a good cook.
alternatives: He cooks well.
He's good at cooking.
point: 「上手」は a good cook か good at -ing

ja: ケンに遊びに来いと言われた。
en: Ken told me to drop by.
alternatives: Ken told me to come by.
Ken told me to come over.
point: tell + 人 + to do。drop by は「ちょっと寄る」

ja: 今日は昨日より暖かい。
en: Today's warmer than yesterday.
alternatives: It's warmer today than yesterday.
Yesterday was colder than today.
point: warmer than で昨日より暖かいと比べる。

ja: 週末はどこへ行ったの？
en: Where'd you go this weekend?
alternatives: Where did you go last weekend?
Where'd you go last weekend?
point: where + did + 主語 + 動詞の原形

ja: 昼ごろにやっと雨が上がった。
en: The rain finally let up around noon.
alternatives: The rain finally eased off around noon.
The rain finally stopped around noon.
point: let up は雨や勢いが弱まる・やむ

ja: 私は最近、近所づきあいを控えてる。
en: I've been socializing less with neighbors lately.
alternatives: I've been cutting back on neighborhood socializing.
I've been keeping neighborly socializing to a minimum.
point: socializing less は付き合いをやめず、量を控えること。

ja: やっと髪を切ってもらった。
en: I finally had my hair cut.
alternatives: I finally got my hair cut.
I finally got a haircut.
point: have + 物 + 過去分詞「〜してもらう」

ja: 私を驚かせたのは町の活気だ。
en: What surprised me was the town's vibrancy.
alternatives: The town's liveliness was what surprised me.
I was surprised by the town's energy.
point: What surprised me was で町の活気が意外で驚いた点を強調する。

ja: 彼女は人の動機が分かると言う。
en: She says she knows what makes people tick.
alternatives: She says she understands what motivates people.
She says she grasps what drives people.
point: what makes people tick は人を動かす心理。

ja: 京都はお寺で有名だよね。
en: Kyoto is known for its temples.
alternatives: Kyoto is famous for its temples.
Kyoto is well known for its temples.
point: 「〜で知られている」は known for

ja: 雨が降ってきたね。
en: It's starting to rain.
alternatives: It's beginning to rain.
It started raining.
point: 降り始めは be starting to で言う

ja: 暑くても、夏が好きなんだ。
en: I love summer despite the heat.
alternatives: I love summer, even though it's hot.
Even with the heat, I love summer.
point: despite の後ろは名詞。文にするなら even though

ja: お昼までには、雨は止んでいたよ。
en: The rain had stopped by noon.
alternatives: By noon, the rain had stopped.
It had stopped raining by noon.
point: 「〜までには」の時点より前は過去完了

ja: 近くに公園があるよ。
en: There's a park nearby.
alternatives: There's a park near here.
There's a park close by.
point: 「〜がある」は there is / there's

ja: ここに座ってもいい？
en: Can I sit here?
alternatives: May I sit here?
Can I take this seat?
point: can I で座る許可を求める。

ja: 今週はずっと暑いね。
en: It's been hot all week.
alternatives: This week has been really hot.
It's been so hot this week.
point: 今週まで続く状態は現在完了

ja: 予報で私は予定を決めずにいた。
en: The forecast had me hedging my bets.
alternatives: The forecast kept me from making plans.
The forecast made me keep my options open.
point: hedge my bets は一つに賭けず選択肢を残す。

ja: 週末はハイキングでもと思ってて。
en: I was thinking of hiking this weekend.
alternatives: I thought I might go hiking this weekend.
I'm thinking about maybe going hiking this weekend.
point: was thinking で決めつけずに柔らかく言う

ja: 電車で、週末の計画を立てたよ。
en: Riding the train, I planned my weekend.
alternatives: I planned my weekend while riding the train.
While on the train, I planned out my weekend.
point: 分詞構文の主語は主節の主語と同じ

ja: 私、朝寝坊が楽しみだ。
en: I'm excited to sleep in.
alternatives: I can't wait to sleep in.
I'm looking forward to sleeping in.
point: sleep in はいつもより遅くまで寝る。

ja: 私、波を眺めたいな。
en: I want to watch the waves.
alternatives: I'd like to watch the waves.
I feel like watching waves.
point: want to do で希望を表す。

ja: 二人で行ったカフェ、良かった。
en: The café we visited was great.
alternatives: The café we went to was great.
The café that we went to was great.
point: 関係詞 that は省略できる。visited は前置詞不要

ja: 近くの人に見覚えがある。
en: Someone nearby seems familiar.
alternatives: Someone close by looks familiar.
I recognize someone nearby.
point: nearby で someone を後ろから説明する。

ja: 君はラッシュを避けるべき。
en: You should avoid rush hour.
alternatives: You ought to avoid rush hour.
You should skip rush hour.
point: rush hour は通勤などで混雑する時間帯。

ja: 傘なしで、きっとびしょ濡れだったね。
en: You must have gotten soaked without an umbrella.
alternatives: You must have been drenched without an umbrella.
Without an umbrella, you must have been soaked.
point: 過去の強い推量は must have + 過去分詞

ja: 私はずっと日差しが恋しい。
en: I've been craving sunshine.
alternatives: I've been longing for sunshine.
I've been missing the sunshine.
point: have been craving はずっと欲しい気持ちが続いている。
